reconstructed_theorem_text:
Let E be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its Borel measurable structure,including dimension zero. Let W:E->R be globally C1 and suppose exp(-W) is Bochner integrable against canonical Lebesgue volume. Define the actual measure
  mu=volume.tilted(x -> -W(x)),
meaning normalized density exp(-W)/integral exp(-W)dvolume relative to volume. The tilt definition alone does not include a probability or nonzero-normalization certificate.
For every real linear partial operator D:L2(mu;R)->L2(mu;E),assume D is closable and that,for all scalar a and vector H L2 classes,
  (a,H) in graph(D) if and only if there exists smooth compactly supported phi:E->R
  with a=phi mu-almost everywhere and H=grad phi mu-almost everywhere.
Then for every real epsilon>0 and every input f in L2(mu;R),there exists u in the domain of T=closure(D) with all of the following properties. Write ubar,fbar for the usual representatives of the scalar classes u,f,and G for the representative of the actual vector class T u.
  (a) For every v in domain(T),with its scalar class and actual vector output T v,
        epsilon <u,v>_{L2(mu;R)}+<T u,T v>_{L2(mu;E)}
          =<f,v>_{L2(mu;R)}.
  (b) ubar:E->R is locally Bochner integrable with respect to volume.
  (c) G:E->E is locally Bochner integrable with respect to volume.
  (d) For every globally C1 compactly supported real psi:E->R and every direction e in E,
        psi(x)<G(x),e> and ubar(x)D psi(x)[e]
      are both integrable against volume,and
        integral psi(x)<G(x),e> dvolume(x)
          =-integral ubar(x)D psi(x)[e] dvolume(x).
  (e) For every globally C1 compactly supported real psi,the following three real integrands are integrable against volume:
        exp(-W(x))(ubar(x)psi(x)),
        exp(-W(x))<G(x),grad psi(x)>,
        exp(-W(x))(fbar(x)psi(x)),
      and the exact weighted test identity holds:
        epsilon integral exp(-W)(ubar psi)dvolume
          +integral exp(-W)<G,grad psi>dvolume
          =integral exp(-W)(fbar psi)dvolume.
The Frechet derivative and gradient of the test functions are actual derivatives. Domain and L2-class coercions use their usual representatives. The unannotated local integrability,Integrable assertions and integrals are with respect to canonical Lebesgue volume;the Hilbert inner products in (a) are instead under the actual mu. The last identity uses the unnormalized weight exp(-W),not an inserted density-normalization factor.
The solution u is fixed before every variational or compact-test quantifier;the same actual T u is used throughout. No uniqueness claim,solution norm bound,mean-zero restriction on f,additional C2 hypothesis on W,dense-domain premise for the supplied D,or existence of D is asserted. Probability normalization of mu is not an extra stated conjunct.
objects: Finite-dimensional real-inner-product Borel E;C1 W and integrable exp(-W);actual tilt mu;scalar/vector L2 quotient spaces;supplied closable exact smooth-gradient partial operator D and closure T;positive epsilon;arbitrary scalar L2 input f;domain solution u,usual scalar representatives ubar/fbar and actual output-vector representative G;L2 variational equation,volume local integrability,unweighted weak-gradient tests and weighted volume test identity.
domains: E has NormedAddCommGroup,InnerProductSpace R,FiniteDimensional R,MeasurableSpace,BorelSpace. W,phi,psi:E->R;mu=volume.tilted(-W). D:Lp R 2 mu partial-linear[R]->Lp E 2 mu. epsilon in R>0;f in scalar L2;u,v in D.closure.domain. G:E->E is representative of D.closure u. Direction e in E. Inner products of quotient classes use mu;all displayed unannotated local/integrable functions and integrals use volume. Zero dimension is permitted.
quantifiers: For every stated E,W satisfying global C1 and exp(-W) volume integrability,define mu. For every D satisfying closability and exact all-a,H graph equivalence,for every epsilon>0 and every scalar L2 input f,there exists one u in closure-domain. This u satisfies the variational equation for every closure-domain v;both local-integrability assertions;the two integrabilities and unweighted weak-gradient identity for every C1 compactly supported psi and every direction e;and the three weighted integrabilities and weighted equation for every such psi. u is chosen before all test quantifiers.
assumptions: W globally ContDiff R 1;exp(-W) Integrable against volume. D is closable and its entire graph is exactly simultaneous mu-a.e. smooth compactly supported scalar function/actual-gradient pairs. epsilon>0;f is arbitrary Lp R 2 mu. E has the stated finite-dimensional inner-product/Borel structures. No C2 W,density certificate,dense-domain premise,mean-zero condition on f or test-membership certificate is supplied.
conclusion: Existence of u in D.closure.domain with the all-domain-vector L2(mu) variational equation;volume LocallyIntegrable scalar representative and actual vector output representative;for every C1 compact test and direction,both unweighted integrabilities and the negative-sign weak-gradient identity;for every C1 compact test,all three exp(-W)-weighted volume integrabilities and the exact weighted epsilon equation. All conjuncts use the same u and actual D.closure u.
scopes: The two measure regimes are distinct:L2 quotient inner products use mu,while local integrability,weak-gradient tests and weighted integrals use canonical volume. The final weight is exp(-W) without division by its partition integral. The supplied D is arbitrary subject to exact graph and closability;the theorem does not construct it or assume dense domain. Test functions are C1 compactly supported,even though initial D graph is specified with smooth compact tests. L2/domain representatives are the actual usual coercions,not pointwise arbitrary new choices. No uniqueness,energy bound,probability conjunct,distributional operator formula beyond the written tests,or numerical process is asserted. No material ambiguity is present.
constant_dependencies: epsilon is any strictly positive real and appears exactly as the scalar multiplier of the L2 inner product and weighted mass integral. The gradient-energy coefficient is exactly 1;the unweighted weak-gradient sign is exactly minus. Tilt density is exp(-W)/integral exp(-W)dvolume,but the displayed weighted equation has unnormalized exp(-W). Lp exponent is 2,C1 tests and smooth graph tests are exact. No further numerical constant or step-size restriction occurs.
